questions.text: A student is developing a program that will store information about players of a video game, including each player's score and amount of time remaining, in seconds. Which of the following is the most appropriate design?

answers.text: An `Information` class with `Player` instance variables for the score and the amount of time remaining
answers.explanation: Puts the data in a separate container class with `Player` fields. The score and time describe one player, so they belong in `Player` itself.

answers.text: A `Player` class with `int` instance variables for the score and the amount of time remaining
answers.explanation: Correct. Score and remaining time are attributes of one player, so a `Player` class with `int` instance variables for them is the natural design.

answers.text: A `Player` class, a `Score` class, and a `RemainingTime` class, each with an `int` instance variable
answers.explanation: Splits each value into its own class that wraps a single `int`. This adds classes without modeling anything new.

answers.text: A `Score` class and a `RemainingTime` class, each with a `Player` instance variable
answers.explanation: Reverses the relationship. A score is a property of a player, so it should not hold a `Player` object.

questions.explanation: Both the score and the remaining time describe one player. A `Player` class with an `int` instance variable for each is the simplest design that matches the problem.

questions.text: Assume that `a`, `b`, and `c` are `boolean` variables that have been properly declared and initialized. Which of the following boolean expressions is equivalent to `!(a && b) || c`?

answers.explanation: Drops the negation. `!(a && b)` is not `a || b`. For example, when both `a` and `b` are false, `!(a && b)` is true but `a || b` is false.
Negates `a` and `b` separately but keeps `&&` between them. De Morgan's law changes the operator to `||`, so this is not equivalent.
Changes the operator to `&&` and requires both `a` and `b` to be false. That does not match the original expression, which is true whenever `c` is true.
Correct. By De Morgan's law, `!(a && b)` is equivalent to `!a || !b`. The whole expression is therefore `!a || !b || c`.

questions.explanation: De Morgan's law says that the negation of an `&&` is the `||` of the negations. So `!(a && b) || c` is the same as `!a || !b || c`.

answers.text: Testing the program with conditions that represent a wide variety of ways the program will be used

answers.text: Using default constructors to set the initial state of the objects used in the program

questions.explanation: Reliability means that a program works correctly in all the ways it is used. Testing with a wide range of conditions is the most direct way to find failures that would otherwise show up only in use.

A programmer wants to investigate whether players of an online game who are younger than 30 years old tend to spend more time playing the game than players who are 30 years old or older. Each player of the game must create an account with a unique username. The programmer has the following data sets available.

- Data set 2 contains an entry for each player. Each entry contains the player's username and the average number of hours the player spends playing the game each day.
- Data set 3 contains an entry for each year since the game was released. Each entry includes the number of players who were born in that year.
- Data set 4 contains an entry for each year since the game was released. Each entry includes a list of usernames of the players who created an account in that year.

Which two data sets can be combined and analyzed to determine the desired information?

Data set 4 groups usernames by the year the account was created. It has no birth dates, so age cannot be found.

questions.explanation: To study age and playing time together, the programmer needs age for each player and playing time for each player. Data sets 1 and 2 share the username field, so they can be joined.
